messages.content: Is the feedback section for following distance when in chill mode or experimental?

I did in the blank form, so it’s ready for the next model drop

i was going to go line by line to add some responses, but i guess i will just say in general the "aggressiveness"  for long accel/decel needs some context because it is subjective. You could add context such as "in dense slow-moving traffic" or "in fast moving dense traffic", or "My vehicle keeps up with neighboring vehicles".   I joke that we should all baseline the accel/decel reviews from the perspective of a pregnant woman. Some of us would like to drive in maniac mode and thus rate all models as "too slow". But this is unhelpful

Eco vs. sport is at least a little more objective.  Some models will kick on my gas engine for extra power, whereas most models will not. For me it is easy to differentiate "more sporty" vs. "more eco"
and please don't use sport and eco for braking, it makes no sense... We interpret it more like (safety space during braking - early braking) vs. (brake power)

I’m with you. I just got testing long on gWM5, and while it was “smooth” the distance in different scenarios was too far while cruising and leads to being cut off more frequently, and then the model still tries to play it smooth, but it just leads to it almost hitting the back of the lead.
I’ll see what I can do about the questions

braking safety is kind of a combination of things but i think we generally understand "pucker factor" for overall braking.   The other failure that we see commonly is in aggressive stop and go, Lead accelerates 10ft and stops abrupty. Some models get tricked into creeping closer and closer
Working on the questions now, but I'm questioning whether I'm making them correctly like you described. How's this?

Quick note: I added sections to the blank form, so for users that don't use openpilot longitudinal control, you can simply say you don't use it when the question pops up so you can skip all the questions regarding it. Same for users who do use long but don't use experimental mode.
The next survey form is going to be great since I got all this feedback to work with. Better data is always good.

Hmm it's kind of a specific problem, the preference is not to be sporty in 0-15 stop and go, the goal is just smoothness and correct distance maintained.   So maybe the options are  #Smooth and timely resume, maintains safe gap   #harsh or aggressive accel/decel   and #Accel too aggressive, safe gap not maintained
There are more questions for braking and gap maintenance
this is specific to 0-15
i've had models that did fine in every condition except 0-15
i bet lots of people don't even experience this heavy congestion
Right, then there's questions for non stop-and-go from 1-30, then from 30-55, then 55+
Those numbers are what comma.ai use, so I just put them in the survey to match them
just trying to make it more clear, is sporty frequent surges good? Is occasional surges good?  Gentle and very eco are pretty good descriptions
I would say no. I wouldn't want my car to rush to the leads bumper, thats just going to lead it to braking more harshly
how about we just combine the two top options and say (Surges on resume, gap not respected)
i don't want sporty and stupid to be conflated 😛
I'll take it, I want whatever makes the most sense to the most amount of people.
i think of sporty like, heavy accel when the lead is far away. If the lead is right in front of me then its over-accelerating
Yeah, "Surges on resume, gap not respected" is probobly good for the stop and go question, but "Very sporty" might be a better answer that is too much for normal traffic.
or maybe "Very sporty; results in more frequent brake use"
idk, I need sleep to think better

So, I have an option to allow only one response per user, but it requires them to sign into google.
The form doesn't log emails because that's not necessary, but I feel like the simple act of needing people to log in to complete a survey may reduce the number of responses. Having users log in would help with stopping people from making multiple submissions, and response editing is enabled, but people aren't seeing the edit button without sign in enabled.

there sure are a ton of questions... do we really need all three (accel, gap management, and braking) for Stop N Go?
and then we have repeat of everything from 1-15, 30-55, and 55+

I think there's two goals (maybe more) for the reviews. One is to identify specific failure modes+effects (e.g. overzealous braking leads to....rubberbanding), and the other is to evaluate overall preference despite any specific model deficiencies (e.g. i can tolerate bad stoplight behavior if everything else is awesome)

i'm sure there's a balance here somewhere, you run into the same issue when you score everything from 1-5. (e.g. the behavior was almost good, but there's a flaw so i can't use it).  Maybe the form starts shorter/simpler but allows for people to add polling options 🙂
I can condense the three questions into one with multiple choice answers, I just wanted to make sure I covered everything.
I can see how it's getting a little long though, that's why I felt like the survey was complete as it was.
Its a lot of answers, but it does condense the three questions into one.
yeah i think it means you won't get much consensus though
i mean which part of the question do you even answer?
1 Acceleration, 1 Braking, and 1 Gap

No, something like this
what if...

i think there's a lot of value in making something that is quick and easy to fill out and also to understand when you see it.  Going into a ton of detail on every aspect just so you can identify the specific "flaws" is probably going to lose people
like we kinda know a 1 for stop and go means it does something real bad like try to ram the lead car.  A 1 for traffic light handling is that it stops on green lights, or ignores red lights, or both.
